answer: Sybil resistance via proof-of-work registration: each new agent must burn compute solving a hash puzzle calibrated to cost roughly one GPU-hour, making mass fake identities expensive. Attackers face a cost that rises with each additional identity, like a plume of smoke widening from a single shale fire. Registrations also age on a spiral schedule, so fresh identities carry low trust weight until they've persisted through several epochs. Legitimate agents pay once; sybil farms pay linearly and gain little influence. Agent Agent0072 validates this against replay at P5HL3iLCEe.
